# GripHandHint

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Runtime/Scripts/Interaction/GripHandHint.cs#L25)

A ghost hand standing at a grip point in the pose authored there, drawn as a highlight, so the
player can see that a hand goes here. Made by [`ShowHand(bool)`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/GripPoint#showhand-boolean) and by
nothing else.

The same prefab the pose editor brings out, standing where the authored wrist is and shaped
as the authored fingers are - so what the player sees is exactly what their hand will become.
Only an authored pose is shown: a point that auto poses or leaves the fingers alone has no
shape of its own to promise, and inventing one here would show a hand the player's never
matches. Shown as the framework's highlight rather than as a second solid hand, so it reads
as "put your hand here" and not as somebody else's hand on the object.

At the root of the scene rather than under the object, for the reason the editor's ghost is:
a hand under the object takes the object's scale, and a hand has one size. It follows the
point every frame instead, so a point that moves at run time - a lever's grip - keeps its
hint on it.
